featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Review for Rustamjee Seasons, BKC

If you’re planning to rent or buy here, I’d strongly say: think twice.

The building looks great on the surface with every amenity listed—gym, pool, squash, TT, yoga rooms—but in practice, it’s a disappointment . Here’s why:
1.	Rigid and impractical rules:
•	Table tennis and squash are restricted with sudden, unclear rules—you can’t just go and play when you want.
•	Gym timings are extremely rigid. Management insists the gym cannot open early because the trainer isn’t available, but ironically, the trainer often shows up an hour late even after the gym has officially opened. Makes no sense.
2.	Amenities without basics:
•	The pool is there, but essential float boards or safety equipment are missing. It’s incomplete and not child-friendly.
3.	Hidden charges everywhere:
•	Even after paying steep rents, almost everything is chargeable—yoga rooms, certain common spaces, and more. Feels unfair and exploitative considering the rent is already high.

On top of this, the hygiene is terrible (toilets stink worse than public ones), lifts are painfully slow, and the management is neither flexible nor approachable. If you’re a tenant, your say is practically zero. Even flat owners don’t have much control since the committee runs on its own agenda. And yes parking is scary-no space to even get into the car-forget your car even being cleaned . I think the list is never ending!

Yes, it’s one of the few residential complexes in BKC, but amenities you can’t use and management you can’t reason with cancel out any advantage.

Verdict: Not worth the rent, not worth the stress. Big no from my side.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Fort is the oldest business district of Mumbai. Fort was the nerve center of the city during the 18th century. Fort George, built by the East India Company around Bombay Castle gave the area its name. The original financial center of the city, fort is home to institutions such as the Bombay Stock Exchange, Reserve Bank of India and Tata Group.

Nariman Point was developed because of space limitations at Mumbai’s original business district, Fort. Built on land reclaimed from the sea, it is named after Khursheed Framji Nariman, a Parsi visionary. Situated at the extreme southern tip of Marine Drive, the area has some of the most expensive office space in the world and is home to some of India’s premier companies.

￼

The Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) was developed to address Mumbai’s growing need for prime commercial space. Built on marshy land reclaimed from the north side of Mahim Creek, Kurla lies to its east and Bandra to the west. BKC is Mumbai’s newest and fastest growing central business district and is planned to serve Mumbai’s needs for prime commercial space for some time to come.

BKC is home to a large number of multinational and Indian conglomerates as well as schools, healthcare facilities, consulates and more.

￼

As a residential destination BKC offers unmatched convenience and a wealth of premium social facilities. The area is home to Mumbai’s premier international schools and educational institutes. BKC is also a diplomatic hub with over 7 consulates. Leading healthcare institutions such as the Asian Heart Hospital provide the best in healthcare in well provided flagship hospitals.

As the leading central business district in India, many blue chip corporate houses and important regulators are headquartered here with many more on their way.

BKC is the ideal location for consulates as it is close to the airport. With huge spaces to expand their operations; consulates like The British deputy high commission and the US consulate have already shifted their administrative offices to BKC. It’s believed that sooner or later, almost all consulates will shift their operations to BKC.

Seamlessly connected and richly appointed, BKC welcomes the connoisse ur with open arms.

￼

A landmark in planned central business districts, the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) is the premier corporate destination of India. A futuristic commercial locality, it is designed at par with global CBDs and is one of the key developments powering Mumbai’s resurgence as a financial and business powerhouse.

The Bandra Worli Sea Link is just a short drive away and connects the area seamlessly to commercial areas such as Lower Parel and Worli. Apart from that, the newly inaugurated Santacruz-Chembur Link Road that connects the Western suburbs with the Central is just a 20 minute drive from BKC. Both the international and domestic airports are a 15 minute drive away while the Western Express Highway provides rapid connectivity to the Northern Suburbs

Disappointing Experience – Poor Facilities and Unresponsive Management
I stayed at The Bombay Home Company for a week, and unfortunately, it was one of the most frustrating hospitality experiences I’ve had.
For the first four days, the air conditioning and jet spray in the bathroom were not functioning — a serious issue given the sweltering summer heat in Mumbai. Despite repeated complaints, the issue remained unresolved. An electrician was sent, but the AC continued to malfunction, leaving me to sleep in an uncomfortably hot room night after night.
After several follow-ups, I was finally offered an alternative accommodation — but it was located 10 kilometers away. No shuttle or assistance was provided for the move, and I had to arrange and pay for transport myself. Upon arrival, I was shocked to find that the new place was not a proper Airbnb apartment, but rather a private room that had been hastily vacated for my stay.
The room reeked of cigarette smoke despite being advertised as non-smoking — a serious concern for someone like me with a smoke allergy. The toilet was unhygienic, the space was extremely cramped, and to make matters worse, the geyser didn’t work. When I reported this, I was told someone would come to fix it, but no one showed up even after an hour.
At that point, I decided to vacate the property and requested a refund for the remaining three days. Not only was my request denied, but the management also stopped responding altogether. When I pointed out that the amenities they failed to provide — working AC, geyser, clean and smoke-free room — were not in line with what was promised, they simply said it was “not in their policy” to offer refunds.
The overall experience was deeply disappointing — from the lack of basic amenities to the unprofessional and indifferent attitude of the staff. I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a comfortable or reliable stay in Mumbai.

Also their sofa had a hole and nail in it which was not visible and i got hurt by that.

featured_reviews.name: AQUIB SHAIKH
featured_reviews.review_text:
Omkar Meridia – Residential apartments near BKC, Mumbai
In the city of Mumbai, living close to the workplace is a dream cherished by many, particularly by those who spend a considerable portion of their time commuting to work. It is not uncommon for people to spend 2 – 3 hours each day traveling between work and home, with the travel time increasing substantially during the rainy season. However, due to the mercurial rise in property prices in Mumbai each year, affordability of residential property near the workplace always remains an issue. In such a scenario, if people can  ‘Walk to work‘, they will not only cut down the long commute and evade agonizing traffic jams, but also gain sufficient time to pursue their interests.
Last week, I had received an invite from Omkar Realtors and Developers to attend an event that included a presentation by the Chief Marketing Officer on Omkar Meridia, a property at BKC Crossing. The event conducted at the property site itself, also included a visit to the sample flat. I registered for the event and reached the venue on the given hour.

The discussion with the CMO centered not only around the property but also around Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), which is an important business hub in the Mumbai suburbs, and the office destination for lakhs of people.  Though there are many commercial establishments and government offices in BKC, at present, there are not enough modern residential developments in and around that area. As a result, majority people who work in BKC do not reside in and around the location, and some have to commute for long hours.

Here I enlist the key points about the property.

Walk to work is the mantra behind the project
Omkar Meridia located at BKC crossing is at an arm’s length from the city’s main business district. It could be an option worth considering for those who work at BKC, and commute from distant suburbs. Proximity to workplace would drastically cut down their commuting time, and thus leave them with sufficient quality time for themselves and their family.

walk-to-work

Social Infrastructure
There are some good schools such as Arya Vidya Mandir, Orchid International School , Mt Litera International School in the vicinity of Omkar Meridia. Health facilities such as Asian Heart Institute, Gurunanak Hospital, Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre are in a 3 km vicinity. Phoenix Market City, is one of the largest shopping malls in Mumbai, too, is close by.

featured_reviews.name: Komal Bagwe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience with L&T Realty has been one of the most disappointing and distressing journeys.

At the time of booking, we clearly communicated that we would pay the full amount only after receiving the Occupancy Certificate (OC). We also paid the initial token amounts as per the payment sheet provided during the booking process. However, without any prior notice, during one of their site visits, Mr. Manan Korani suddenly told my parents that they must pay ₹25 lakhs for both flats within 2–3 days — or the company would cancel the flats.

He stated that if we canceled voluntarily on the spot, no penalty would be applied, but if the company initiated the cancellation, charges would be imposed. My parents — who were handling everything alone while my sister and I were abroad — were confused and pressured, and were asked to sign a blank cancellation form without name or date. This felt like the company was taking advantage of their situation.

Only after involving a lawyer and sending a formal mail did they reverse their stance and say we could pay post-OC — exactly as initially agreed.

But the problems didn’t end there. We had booked a jodi (combined) apartment — a merged unit shown to us and committed by Mr. Prashant Sawant and Mr. Chetan Balsara. We were even provided the interior layout based on the combined structure. Now, we are suddenly being told that the flats will be handed over as two separate units, and that we must handle the merging ourselves — a complete breach of transparency.

Every visit brings a new shock, and the experience has been mentally exhausting. For a brand like L&T, this kind of unprofessionalism, lack of transparency, and harassment is beyond disappointing. And frankly, we now fear what more issues or pressure tactics we may face until the actual handover of the flat.
